Introduction of the County and About This Article

This guide explains how property tax sales are handled in Ray County, Missouri. It is made to help people who want to understand how the county handles delinquent tax sales for real estate. You will find answers to when sales are held, how to take part, where they are held, and how the bidding process works. This guide also tells you where to find updates and who to contact for help. The aim is to present clear, easy-to-read information so you can plan your next steps with confidence.

What Is/Brief Overview of County’s Tax Lien Investing

When property taxes go unpaid in Ray County, the county can sell a certificate or the right to collect those taxes at a public auction. This sale is done to recover the taxes that are owed. Investors can bid to pay those taxes in exchange for a certificate of purchase. The owner of the property then has a chance to pay the owed amount plus interest to redeem the property. If the owner does not redeem, the investor may seek a deed to the property after following state law. Missouri law governs how taxes become delinquent and how the sales are run.

Important Details

Key Takeaways
  • This guide provides information on property tax sales in Ray County, Missouri, covering the process for delinquent taxes.
  • Delinquent tax sales occur annually in August at the Ray County Courthouse, starting at 10 AM.
  • Investors must register with the Ray County Collector to participate, and the redemption period lasts up to one year.
  • Bidders can earn interest if property owners redeem their properties or potentially acquire properties if owners do not redeem.
  • Due diligence in researching properties is crucial to mitigate risks and ensure informed bidding.

When and Where Are Tax Sales Held?

In Ray County, delinquent tax sales are normally held each year in August on a Monday morning. The sale starts in the late morning at about 10 AM Central Time at the Ray County Courthouse, where the collector’s office is located.

The courthouse address is:

Ray County Courthouse
100 West Main Street, Suite 12
Richmond, Missouri 64085

This is where bidders gather to register and take part in the live auction that offers properties with unpaid taxes.

Is Registration Required to Participate?

Yes. Before you can bid at the tax sale in Ray County, you must register with the Ray County Collector of Revenue’s office. Registration is necessary so the office can validate your eligibility to bid and provide a bidder packet if needed. The collector’s office can also answer questions about required documentation and deadlines for registration.

When Does Registration Start and End?

Registration typically opens several weeks before the tax sale and closes shortly before the auction begins on the day of the event. You should contact the Ray County Collector’s Office to learn the exact registration window for the upcoming sale. They will provide details about forms, fees, and any identification or affidavits that must be completed.

You can reach the Collector at:

Email: rcc@collector.raycountymo.gov
Phone: (816) 776-2187

How Long Is the Redemption Period?

In Missouri, most counties give the former owner up to one year to redeem their property after a tax sale by paying the amount owed plus interest and any costs. This is set by state statute and applies to most first and second offerings in a county sale.

This means you do not immediately own the property after the sale. The owner can pay what is owed during the redemption period and keep the property.

How the Bidding Procedure Works

At the Ray County tax sale, the county offers each parcel of real estate with unpaid taxes to the public. Here is how the sale usually works:

  • The auction begins with the first property on the list.
  • Each parcel is read out with a legal description by the auction official.
  • Bidders offer amounts above the total owed taxes, penalties, and costs.
  • Bidding continues until no more higher offers are made.
  • The highest bidder wins the certificate of purchase for that property.

You must pay the full amount you bid either the same day or according to the collector’s payment instructions. Once the amount is paid, you receive a Certificate of Purchase. This gives you rights to collect interest or move toward title after the redemption period expires.

Under Missouri law, after winning, you may apply for a collector’s deed if the owner does not redeem within the permitted time.

Who Should Be Contacted for More Information

For official details about registration, lists of properties, redemption rules, or deadlines, contact:

Ray County Collector of Revenue
Email: rcc@collector.raycountymo.gov
Phone: (816) 776-2187
Address: Ray County Courthouse, 100 W Main St, Richmond, MO 64085

This office manages the tax sale process and is the best source for up-to-date forms and notices.

Where to Find Updates on Upcoming Tax Sales

Updates about tax sales and related deadlines can be found:

  • On the Ray County Collector’s official website: https://raycountycollectormo.com/
  • On the Ray County government site: https://raycountymo.com/
  • In local newspapers where legal notices are published before the sale.
  • By calling or emailing the collector’s office for the most current notices and property lists.

Fun Facts About Ray County

  • Ray County is in northwest Missouri around Kansas City but more rural in feel.
  • Richmond is the county seat and home to historic sites and local events.
  • The county has a mix of farmland, small towns, and residential neighborhoods.
  • The county assessor’s office provides public property searches online.

Attractions & Economic Highlights

  • Historic Sites: Local museums and historic buildings around Richmond.
  • Parks and Outdoor Space: Green areas and nature trails for visitors.
  • Transportation: Major highways connect Ray County to larger markets.
  • Economy: Farming, small manufacturing, retail trade, and services support local jobs.

Why This County is Ideal for Tax Investors

  • High returns are possible when owners redeem with interest under state rules.
  • A one-year redemption period gives investors time to plan next moves.
  • Missouri tax law allows active investor participation.
  • Properties range across rural and town markets offering investment variety.

These points show why tax sale investing in Ray County can be a low-risk investment when done with proper research.

Auction Process for Tax Lien Sales

How the Auction Works

  1. Arrive early at the courthouse.

  2. Check in and confirm bidder registration.

  3. Listen for property descriptions.

  4. Bid on parcels you researched.

  5. Pay for your bid once you win.

This process is common to most Missouri county tax sales.

Maximum Potential & Expected Returns

When a property is sold, investors may earn interest if the owner redeems. The expected return depends on how long it takes for redemption and how much interest accrues under state law. If the owner does not redeem, investors may secure a deed, which can enhance investment return when property is resold or developed.

Open to All Investors / Foreign Investor Participation

Missouri tax sales are open to all legal bidders, including out-of-state and foreign investors who register and meet requirements. This provides global investment opportunities for those with funds and understanding of local tax sale laws.

Importance of Due Diligence in Tax Investing

What Due Diligence Entails

  • Search property ownership and tax history.
  • Inspect property location and condition when possible.
  • Check for liens and title issues at the assessor and recorder’s offices.
  • Verify property details before you bid.

Risks of Skipping Research

  • Unknown liens and costs may add expenses.
  • Some properties may be hard to sell or develop.
  • Redemption may erase your claim if the owner pays.

Thorough research helps reduce risks and gives you a clearer investment picture.

Conclusion

Tax sales in Ray County provide a way for investors to bid on liens for properties with unpaid taxes. Sales are held each August beginning around mid-morning at the county courthouse. Bidders must register before sale day. Owners can redeem their property within a year. With careful research and planning, investors may earn returns through interest or property acquisition. Always consult the collector’s office for current lists, requirements, and sale notices before you bid.
